title: Relief drumming in the district and Blue Monday at the 25
summary: He relieved Cottrell at Rice, Zeno at Pete Lala's and others, and recalls the ham-kicking contest at the 25.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: That's right. Right. That's right. You hit the first note on the right foot? Yeah, right on the right foot, yeah. What places did you play in the district? Oh, in the district? Let me see. I worked at, I didn't work regular. I mean I, I relief old man Contrell at Rice. I used to relief him there. And then I relief Henry Zeno at Pete Lala. I used to relief him there. When King Oliver had the band, Joe Oliver had the band. He wasn't King then. It was Joe, Joe Oliver. And then I played at Few Clothes a few times. And I forget what drummer it was I reliefed there. He was an old time drummer. Oh yeah. It was Ernest Rogers, that's right. Ernest Rogers, that's right. I had a few clothes and then I, and I worked at the 101 Ranch. That was next block from Few Clothes. That was on Franklin between Iverville and Bimble. That's where Krauss's Warehouse was at, something there. Pete Lala's wasn't 25, so was that, that's that job? No, 25, no, it was a different place, no, 25. Pete Lala's. 25, 25, been there before Pete Lala came in existence. 25 used to be placed at the, on the Monday I mean used to be Blue Monday here. What was that? Oh, on the Blue Monday I mean nobody was awake on Monday. People said it was Blue Monday, they'd have a good time. They lay off. And 25 would always have a crowd there. And they would give a prize. They had a ham, used to hang a string of ham up. And they'd come down certain height and at a contest, a woman that could kick the ham, would win a prize. I don't know what the prize was. But I mean she'd win a prize, kick the ham. They had that every Monday there. They did? Yeah, I was, I was, I was. Was it in the back room where the pool tables and? No, no, I can't say it was. I mean, no, that part I can't say. Because I was allowed to go in there. I was too young to go in there. I remember they used to kick the ham then. This was for, for the women? For the women, yeah. Kick the ham. That sounds pretty good. You get to, get to see what kind of legs they got. I expected that was the reason for the game, wasn't it? Yeah, I mean, I'm sure.
